paragraphs.text: The printing press made public debate possible in early modern Europe. Cheap pamphlets let ordinary readers take sides.
Books became cheaper after 1450, and more people could read them. Many historians say literacy rose, but it is hard to know how fast.
Pamphlets spread news quickly, readers in different cities could argue about the same events. This helped people share ideas.
Debate in print was not new, but its reach was.
